items.content_html:
Description

Adds new guide Web/HTML/Guides/Processing_instructions covering DOM representation (ProcessingInstruction / CharacterData), syntax, XML vs HTML parsing differences (optional trailing ?, target regex [A-Za-z_][-_A-Za-z0-9]*, reserved xml/xml-stylesheet to comment), and declarative out-of-order patching with <template for> (<?marker> and <?start>/<?end>). Adds cross-links from Web/API/ProcessingInstruction and Web/HTML/Reference/Elements/template.

Placed under HTML per discussion (Josh-Cena: "shouldn't be in DOM; it should be in HTML") and ddbeck's recommendation in mdn/browser-compat-data#30292 - BCD PR intentionally removed per-marker api.ProcessingInstruction.marker-* keys and deferred documentation to prose/guide.

Motivation

Fixes #45309. Currently processing instructions are only documented under the Web/API/ProcessingInstruction reference page (Description section) with no dedicated guide. With Declarative Partial Updates (<template for>) in Chrome 150 making <?start>/<?marker>/<?end> more visible in HTML (https://developer.chrome.com/blog/declarative-partial-updates#out-of-order_streaming), a discoverable guide explaining what PIs are, how HTML parsing differs from XML, and how they relate to both the DOM API and <template> patching was requested.

Additional details

  • New page: files/en-us/web/html/guides/processing_instructions/index.md (slug: Web/HTML/Guides/Processing_instructions, page-type: guide, sidebar: htmlsidebar, spec-urls: https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/parsing.html#processing-instruction-target-state, https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#processinginstruction)
  • Scope intentionally narrow (PI definition, syntax, DOM, HTML vs XML, template patching, limitations) - not a general HTML/XML rendering guide per reviewer feedback
  • No new BCD keys - html.elements.template.for implicitly covers markers as decided in mdn/browser-compat-data#30292 (comment mdn/browser-compat-data#30292 (comment))
  • Related spec: https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/parsing.html#processing-instruction-target-state, https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#processinginstruction, https://www.w3.org/TR/xml/#sec-pi

Related issues and pull requests

Fixes #45309
Relates to mdn/browser-compat-data#30292
Relates to mdn/browser-compat-data#30213 (precedent for PI data handling)
Relates to #45104 (Usage with <template for> example)
Relates to #45315 (<template for> content)
Relates to web-platform-dx/web-features#4073 / #4265
items.title: Add Processing Instructions guide (Fixes #45309)

Description

Explain that listeners registered after a resource loads miss its load event, and show the guarded image check suggested in the issue. Set the live example's source after registering its handler so initial loads and the Reload button both work.

A separate test commit builds four expected diagnostic paths with path.join so the existing front matter assertions work on Windows as well as Unix. Error text and content assertions are unchanged.

Motivation

Readers need to handle images that finish loading before their scripts run without processing the same image twice or treating a failed image as loaded.

Additional details

Verified the extracted examples in Chrome with eight checks covering a missed late event, already loaded and pending images, duplicate callback prevention, failed and missing sources, and initial and repeated loads. The duplicate event check uses a synthetic event. The local harness serves an image fixture in place of the shared MDN asset.

The page build passed with warnings treated as errors. Repository precommit checks, spelling and diff checks passed. All 12 unit tests pass on Windows after the expected paths were made portable. Signing and hooks remain enabled.

The prepush full documentation build also completed successfully. It reported 698 issues across 241 pages; the focused build of this changed page reported none.

Related issues and pull requests

Fixes #44591

Description

This change updates the theme manifest key with you screenshot images and other changes introduced by nova in Firefox 157.

Notes on requested changes

Note which keys render differently in Nova (Firefox 157+), for example tab bar colour applied to the toolbar with vertical tabs.

  • This example doesn’t seem to represent a difference; the tab related color properties I’ve tested apply to horizontal and vertical tabs pre-Nova and Nova

Sidebar keys: what each one affects, and known gaps such as panel hover states not following the theme (bug 2048674).

  • Unclear from the bug which theme color properties this affects, link to the example theme in the bug doesn’t obviously resolve to a theme extension example

Selected-tab keys and the removed Proton shadow (bug 2051102).

  • Note added to tab_selected

theme_frame behaviour behind the sidebar (bug 2043655).

  • No change made in here. The theme developer can address this issue by adding a fade to the bottom of their image. A similar situation is discussed regarding images displayed in the top toolbar in the Extension Workshop article. I’ll look to extend that to cover images bleeding into the sidebar

New popup_icons colour once bug 2064645 lands, including its browser-compat-data entry.

  • Still open; no changes here

A short note on compatibility: unknown colour properties are ignored by older Firefox versions; use strict_min_version for features that need a newer Firefox.

  • Note added. However, based on the information provided so far, there don’t appear to be any new Nova-only color properties.

Updated example images where they show the browser.

  • New images added throughout

Notes on observed key behavior

Not working in Nova

  • ntp_text: Text in the new tab page search box is styled, but isn’t styled in Nova.
  • popup_text: Previously applied to the URL bar dropdown, but in Nova it keeps its default text color. Applies to other popups as expected in Nova (only bookmark popup checked).
  • sidebar_highlight: Visible highlight effect in Pre Nova/Documented, but in Nova the default highlight color is used and this key has no visible effect.
  • sidebar_highlight_text: Worked in Pre Nova/Documented, but in Nova there is no highlighting for selected items and it has no visible effect.

Changed pre-Nova

  • sidebar_border: Documented as styling a splitter and the sidebar border, but the splitter feature appears removed.
  • toolbar_bottom_separator: Previously styled the bottom edge of the toolbar, but now it functions as a right/bottom toolbar separator or page frame separator. Works as previously; improved description to reference sidebar

Not working (current and Nova)

  • tab_loading: Highlighted indicator during tab load in the documented version, not styled in current or Nova.

Description

Added documentation describing the server-side requirements for WebTransport over HTTP/3 including how the client establishes a session with a server.

The WebTransport API documentation explains how a client connects to a server, but did not explain what is required on the server side or what the URL represents.

This adds enough server-side context to help readers understand how a WebTransport connection is established and where to find implementations for different languages, without documenting a complete server implementation.

items.content_html:
There is ongoing confusion with how permissions-policy delegation works - such as #45166. This was an attempt to capture how this works at top level.

The summary basically goes

  • if a top level document has a Permissions-Policy for a feature, the features allowlist defines the superset of origins that it can delegate to in an iframe.
    • The feature must also be delegated by the allow attribute - i.e. listed in the attribute or covered by the allowlist of something like *.
    • The default allowlist is used for delegation if allow is not specified. So if no allow is specified and the default allowlist is self, a frame that specifies a self origin will automatically get the permission.
  • But if the top level document does NOT have a Permissions-Policy for a feature no restrictions are placed on delegation.
    • Nothing stops you from delegating a permission the parent has to any origin it likes, as long as that is specified in allow (as long as the parent has that permission, which is does by default for everything except unload).
    • Note that the default allowslist is still used to define the default origins for granting - i.e. self or *.

@wbamberg Hope this is helpful

Description

Update the live device orientation example to request permission from a button click when DeviceOrientationEvent.requestPermission() is available. Show the permission result in the example and start listening only after permission is granted. Browsers without that method can start the example from the same button without a permission request.

Also clarify the separate permission example's comment: exposing the request method does not mean the browser will necessarily prompt.

Motivation

The previous documentation-only approach in #45809 was closed after maintainer feedback. The live example itself needs to request permission and expose the result so readers can distinguish denied access from an unresponsive sensor.

Additional details

Local checks: MarkdownLint, Prettier, CSpell, changed-file pre-commit hooks, and four executed example behavior tests passed (granted, denied, unsupported method, rejected request).
